title: Navigator
loss_summary: Asset, reputation, and process loss after a Dover Strait grounding.
narrative: Container vessel grounding at Verne Bank in the Dover Strait. The worked solution highlights route-monitoring failure, missed warnings, wrong ECDIS settings, and an unserviceable audible alarm, then traces the event back to weak supervision, poor bridge leadership, and defect-reporting failures.
recommendations: Lessons learned: navigation is critical and familiarisation must be supervised. Immediate actions: issue a fleet bulletin, send type-specific ECDIS refresher support, and run extraordinary navigation-safety audits. System actions: strengthen competence management, formalise training-provider review, and add independent navigational safety assurance.

title: Sinkfast
loss_summary: People, asset, and environmental loss after a pump-room explosion.
narrative: Tanker pump-room explosion at Esso Fawley with one fatality. The worked solution shows permit-to-work weaknesses, poor gas-detection practice, unsafe task assignment for a new joiner, defective detection equipment, and ignition-source control failures, then ties those to competence, supervision, maintenance, and management-of-change gaps.
recommendations: Lessons learned: the company did not identify the full Management of Change impact when it took a new vessel type into management. Immediate actions: issue a safety bulletin, revise the SMS with third-party support, overhaul pumps, repair ventilation, and calibrate gas detection before sailing. System actions: raise tanker competence requirements, revise the competence matrix, improve crew retention, and place experienced tanker management ashore.
